messages:
Maya Rivera: Hi team, quick onboarding snag: I duplicated the "Runbook - Incident" template but it doesn't show in the org templates gallery. I followed the PR flow doc but wonder if I missed a step — who owns the canonical library and what tags are required?
Harper DevEx: welcome Maya! The canonical gallery is curated by the Docs Maintainers. Duplicating to your workspace is fine, but to appear in the gallery you need a docs-templates PR and the maintainer to merge it.
Maya Rivera: ok. I filed a PR (link pasted in repo) but the PR checks failed with a Notion sync error: "page-metadata-mismatch". Is there a required top-level property format?
Jonah Docs Maintainer: hey Maya, thanks for filing. The metadata must be a simple property table at the top with exact keys: template (yes), owner (team name), visibility (org/team), category (runbook/onboarding/howto), last-reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD). The sync checks are strict. If any key is missing or spelled differently the sync rejects it.
Maya Rivera: doh — I used "team-owner" instead of "owner". I'll update. Quick Q: can maintainers rename tags during merge or do you prefer contributors to fix?
Jonah Docs Maintainer: we can fix minor tag typos but prefer contributors update the page so audit history is clear. Also keep the page in the Eng space while drafting; moving it between workspaces can break the sync.
Priya People Ops: small onboarding tip: for checklists, include a linked property "Assignee" that points to People Ops board so we can auto-assign tasks on day 1. If you want your runbook referenced from onboarding, add a linked relation to the "Team runbooks" database.
Maya Rivera: thanks — the page is currently in my personal workspace. Should I move it to Eng space before updating metadata?
Jonah Docs Maintainer: yes, move it to Eng > Templates > Drafts. Then add the property table. Also make sure any code blocks labeled as "example" aren't locked if we expect people to copy commands. Locked command blocks are allowed but document why.
Maya Rivera: got it. Another odd thing: the PR check complained about mentions like @oncall not resolving. I used the group mention in the page.
Harper DevEx: group mentions often don't resolve after sync because the page namespace changes. Best practice: use descriptive text like "@oncall (replace with your team group)" and add a comment with the rotation link. Maintainers will patch or flag unresolved mentions during review.
Maya Rivera: one last ask: is there a way to request Docs Maintainers to do a quick review before I open a PR? This was my first time and the sync errors were cryptic.
Jonah Docs Maintainer: sure — drop the Notion link in a draft message to #devex and tag us with "review-request". We can do a 10-min pre-check to catch common issues. Also include a one-line summary and the desired visibility (org/team) in the message.
notion-sync-bot: PR check result for PR#42: failed  reason: page-metadata-mismatch; unresolved-mentions. See checklist at https://redwood.notion.site/devex/template-sync-checklist.
Maya Rivera: thanks everyone — I'll move the page to Eng drafts, fix the metadata, replace group mentions, and request a pre-review in #devex. Appreciate the help! :raised_hands:
